dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Jammu and Kashmir (Extension of Laws) Act, 1956

Key Provisions:
1.	Extension of Central Laws 
o	The Act empowered the Central Government to extend certain laws enacted by Parliament to Jammu and Kashmir. 
o	The extended laws became applicable to the State subject to modifications and adaptations specified in the Act. 
2.	Application with Modifications 
o	The Central Government could make necessary adaptations and modifications while extending laws to ensure their effective implementation in Jammu and Kashmir. 
o	Such modifications were intended to suit the administrative and constitutional conditions of the State. 
3.	Amendment and Repeal of Existing Laws 
o	The Act provided for necessary amendments or repeals of inconsistent provisions in existing laws. 
o	It helped avoid conflicts between extended Central laws and State laws.
